reference_items.path_to_ten: Three named repairs, all small. (1) Stop the -1 sentinel colliding with a rebased death frame: carry camera.deathFrame as an explicit {active:boolean, frames_ago:int} pair, or clamp at restore rather than at serialise, so save->load->save is a fixed point at every point of the death window; add a mid-death pre-roll to tools/journey/state-diff.mjs so the check can fail. (2) Resolve nested move references the same way pose.move is resolved — fight.*.pendingReaction.move must go through the same slot-id lookup. (3) Make sim.progression.gold the single authority for the purse: have Engine.setGold, parley applyAccept, travelRide and the fence write back to it, or serialise combat.world.gold directly; then extend getDurableFieldCensus()'s shot() to walk engine.combat.world, engine.crime, engine.travel and sim._traversal so a register with no writer cannot round-trip clean again.

ARBITRATION S6 gives Morrowind the save semantics and requires that quest state, journal, faction standing and world flags persist untouched through a death. Two separate S6 failures were measured, both on the death transition. (1) A save taken inside the death window does not round-trip at all: pose.camera_death_frames_ago collapses to the -1 'never died' sentinel, so which death you are in is destroyed by the save — 24 of 36 trials, 4 of 4 states. (2) The death runtime's own timers are restored unrebased: death.controllable_at stays at 161 while the frame resets to 0, so a player who reloads 137 frames into a death waits the full 161 again, on 10 of 10 seeds.

ARBITRATION §1 (as amended) gives Morrowind the right to yield, parley or BRIBE inside a fight, and game/src/combat/parley.js:97 tests that ground as (world.gold || 0) >= enemy.parley.gold_price. On helstrom-market, rootlands-well-graph and stormhold-street, world.gold is 600 before a save and 0 after — so an inf_trash (gold_price 180) can be bought off before the load and cannot be after, with no other state changed. A Morrowind exit from a Souls fight is deleted by a save/load, which is Morrowind losing ground inside the fight.
getTravelState().gold reads the same destroyed register: 600 -> 0 on 10 of 10 seeds on stormhold-street, so a fare a player could afford before a save is refused after it.
No objective marker, bonfire warp, procedural loot or soul-currency purchase is introduced by the save path.

score.band_label: Wrong shape — capped by a triggered hard fail (SCORING §1.1)

biggest_gap.what: The gold a player can actually spend is held in `combat.world.gold` (rebuilt by `Engine._buildCombat`) and `sim.stealth.p.gold`, and neither is ever written back into `sim.progression.gold` — the only gold register the save carries. On 3 of the 38 shipped named states (helstrom-market, rootlands-well-graph, stormhold-street) a plain save/load destroys 600 gold, on 10 of 10 seeds, and it survives a real cold reload through IndexedDB as well. Every shipped instrument reports clean while it happens: M1 hash equal, M2 diff empty, M4 set difference empty both ways, `getDurableFieldCensus().ok` true, and the M5 trace byte-identical. Falsified with the null control — blanking `progression.gold` and `fight.loadout.gold` out of the blob produces exactly the same world as leaving them alone, which is CONSUMPTION coupling 0 on a field this very repair added to the manifest.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: A player who walks into Helstrom market with 600 gold, saves, and comes back a week later has been robbed of it, and the bribe that ARBITRATION §1 guarantees as a non-lethal exit from a fight is refused for want of money they still believe they have.

remedy.action: Make one register the authority for the purse and give the save that register, then widen the census so the class of defect cannot recur. (a) In `game/src/engine.js`, have `setGold`, `combat/parley.js applyAccept` (`world.gold -= spent`), `travelRide` (`world.gold -= fare`), `fenceSell`/`bribeWitness` (`stealth.p.gold`) and the capture path all write through to `sim.progression.gold`, and have `_buildCombat` read only from it — or, if the three registers must stay, serialise `combat.world.gold` and `sim.stealth.p.gold` as their own manifest paths under Progression with the same rebase discipline the rest of the group uses. (b) Extend `Engine.getDurableFieldCensus()`'s `shot()` to clone `this.combat.world`, `this.travel`, `this.crime`/`sim.stealth`, `this.conversation` and `sim._traversal` — it currently walks a declared subset and its own comment warns that 'a census that walks a subset of the simulation is an instrument that certifies a subset'. (c) Add a save point with money in it to `tools/journey/state-diff.mjs`'s pre-roll, so the sweep can fail.
remedy.acceptance: On helstrom-market, rootlands-well-graph and stormhold-street, at ten seeds: `getTravelState().gold` and `getCombatState().world_knowledge.gold` are unchanged across `saveRoundTrip()` AND across a `writeSave` + page reload + `readSave`; and `node tools/harness/save-break-critic.mjs` reports `no-gold` as `detected_by_any_shipped_instrument: true` — that is, blanking the purse out of the blob now makes at least one of M1, M4 or the census go red.

secondary_observations.what: The builder's own falsifier verifies: re-running `tools/harness/save-break.mjs` unmodified gives 8/8 with `baseline_clean: true` and `applied: true` on every break, in ONE run rather than the two the builder needed. The three breaks it reported as 'failing to take' in round 2 — creation-terms (blanked two arrays already empty on a state with no character), no-body-grid (nudged 1e-9, three orders below the 6-dp grid) and no-stamp-rebase (guarded on an already-expired stamp) — all take in their rewritten form. The rewrites are honest: each names why the first version could not have taken, and creation-terms carries its own observer because blanking a field in the blob makes save == load == blanked and the round-trip diff can never see it. I found no break that had been rewritten to make itself pass.

A save taken in mid-air is lethal. Falling 40 m from `default`, the never-saved control lands at hp 620 and the arm that saved and loaded mid-fall lands at hp 0 — dead — because `Engine._buildCombat` constructs a fresh MagicSystem on every load and `magic.airborne`, `magic.fall.velMps` and `magic.peakY` are a second fall model that is not on the manifest at all. Reproduced 6/6 across three seeds with the two arms run in both orders. The manifest's Traversal group carries `airborne`, `vy` and `apex_y`; the model that actually resolves the landing does not.

The death surface restarts on every load. `death.controllable_at` (161) and `death.death_frame` / `death.deaths[].frame` / `death.last_damage_frame` (11) are restored raw while `loadState()` resets the frame to 0, so `surface_frames_left` goes 137 -> 161 on 10 of 10 seeds. The Death state group on the manifest is one path — `death.bloodstain` — and the death runtime is not in the save; it only appears to survive a warm load because nothing clears it, which is why a cold reload is a different test.

The manifest's `rules.dynamic_containers` list exempts 20 paths from M4's set difference by declaring them leaves, and five of them are the repair's own additions (`fight.player`, `fight.player_ctl`, `crime.bounty`, `crime.zones`, `world.capture`, `progression.sap_taint`). That is not falsification — the note declares it and points at the census — but it does mean the set difference the item calls its completeness check does not look inside the combat body at all, and the census that is supposed to cover it walks `sim.*` and the bodies and not `engine.combat.world`, `engine.crime`, `engine.travel`, `engine.conversation` or `sim._traversal`. The purse fell into exactly that hole.

Two of the identity-valued declarations cannot be driven off their identity by anything a player can do, so they round-trip perfectly and carry nothing. `traversal.breath_s` stays at 60.0 and `traversal.submerged` stays false after 3,000 frames of swimming in 40.3 m of water in band W5 — the character floats and never dives — so the repair's headline claim that 'a save taken drowning reloaded with a full lungful' describes a state the build cannot reach. `player.burdenRatio` stayed 0 under `setEquipLoad(30)` because it is recomputed from inventory weight every step by `_recomputeBurden()`, making it derived rather than durable. Both are harmless today and both are places a false pass will live.

NEGATIVE EVIDENCE, recorded because the repair deserves it. The traversal restore is real: with breath perturbed to 3.25, mire to 0.77, slide to 4.5 and vy to -12.5 by hand, loading the blob put all four back exactly. The nine non-death scenarios came back clean on all ten seeds — including mid-cast, mid-parry and a save taken inside an active hitbox window, which the builder's own pre-roll does not reach — with 1,239 to 1,530 live-world leaves compared per trial and zero differing. M3, which the builder never ran, passes on four states across a real page reload through IndexedDB.

`loadState('<named state>')` does not reset every live subsystem, so a scenario inherits the one before it inside a single page. Three of five province scenarios (in-water, mid-fall, mid-travel) failed my instrument's own reproducibility control — two identical pre-rolls, no save and no load between them, produced different player positions and, in one case, a live player in one arm and a corpse in the other. This is the same contamination family the repair itself found and closed for `sim.captured`; it is not closed for the fall model or the traversal. It also means any critic running two arms in one page on a province state is measuring contamination unless it checks.

method_deviations.deviation: Wrote and used `tools/journey/save-live-audit.mjs` instead of `tools/journey/state-diff.mjs` as the primary round-trip instrument.
method_deviations.why: state-diff.mjs was written by the agent whose repair it grades, and every one of its headline checks (M1, M2, M4) is taken on the save BLOB — M1 is a fixed-point test on the serialiser, so a field written to the blob and never read back still passes whenever it re-serialises to the value that was saved. The new tool never reads the blob: it observes the world through ~30 public harness getters, in two arms (control vs save+load) plus a two-run reproducibility control, and classifies every numeric leaf twice (absolute and frame-relative) so a stamp restored unrebased is reported rather than excluded by a list. It also uses pre-rolls the builder's single pre-roll does not reach: mid-cast, mid-parry, mid-death, mid-menu, mid-travel, in water, mid-fall, at a hearth, mid-crime-hunt. Its two declared exclusions (`first_input`/`first_control`, and `.const.`/`.budget.`/`.declared` data constants) are in the report file with their reasons.

method_deviations.deviation: Wrote and used `tools/harness/save-consume-critic.mjs` alongside, not instead of, the builder's `tools/harness/save-consume.mjs`.
method_deviations.why: TOOL-LOOP rule 3 and the tool critic's standing finding: a self-test written by the same hand proves less than an independent falsification. Its P3 probe deliberately runs the BUILDER'S OWN `__HARNESS.saveRoundTrip()` so the 24-of-36 M1 failure cannot be blamed on my instrument.

method_deviations.deviation: Wrote and used `tools/harness/save-break-critic.mjs` — four breaks the builder's eight-break falsifier does not contain, each asking not only whether the failure returns but which of the build's own shipped instruments notices.
method_deviations.why: A repair whose deletion no shipped instrument can see is a repair nobody can regress-test, and a manifest row whose deletion changes nothing is accommodation rather than agreement (RI-JRN05 'How we lose' #7 and #8). This is what found the purse.

method_deviations.deviation: M11, M13, M14, M15, M18, M19, M6, M7, M9 not run; M12, M16, M17 run in part.
method_deviations.why: Wall clock on a four-core box shared with other agents. Every one is recorded `unmeasurable` and fail-closed rather than assumed, per SCORING §1.1. They do not change the item's score, which is already capped at 2 by HF1.

self_audit.self_audit_note: Nine of the item's nineteen methods were not run and are recorded `unmeasurable`, fail-closed, in `method_deviations` and in the checks array; the reason is wall clock on a shared four-core box, not a judgement that they would pass. notes:
AR-3 (seam sterility): NOT sterile. This piece carries at least three live crossings, and two of them are where it fails. `combat/parley.js` reads a WORLD register (`world.gold`) to decide whether a Souls fight has a Morrowind exit; `crime.zones` and the guard search read a world ledger into enemy behaviour; and the fight's loadout is restored from the same blob that carries the journal. `seam_sterile: false`. The AR-2 failure above is a seam failure in the strict sense: the Morrowind half's money is destroyed by the save and the consequence lands inside the Souls fight.

On the builder's headline claim: 76/76 does NOT survive. The number is real for what it measured — I could not break the nine non-death scenarios at ten seeds — but the sweep it comes from applies ONE pre-roll to all 38 states, and that pre-roll never dies, never falls and never holds money. Widening the seeds from two to ten changed nothing; widening the MOMENT changed everything. Two seeds was not the weakness here; one pre-roll was.

On W1-00 and W1-00-r2: both scored RI-JRN05 at 2 with HF1 triggered, and both predate this repair. This verdict re-scores the item at 2 with HF1 triggered again, for a different cause. The repair is substantial and much of it is real — see the negative-evidence observation — but the item's band admits nothing below a perfect round trip, and the round trip is not perfect.
